Hi everyone—since I’m new, let me buy lunch and propose an April newcomer’s bonus for the four of you: John, Kate, Jack, and Emma each catch 15 tons this month, and I’ll take zero. That gives each of you $15,000, with none of the catch going to me.

Your combined 60-ton catch would leave 40 tons, which doubles to 80 next month. It’s more than we can sustainably take every month, so I’m proposing it as a one-time bonus, not our permanent quota. Next month we could cap the combined catch at 30 tons, leaving 50 to reproduce back to 100.

For this to work as proposed, please each actually select 15 tons when you make your private harvest decision—don’t count on someone else taking the bonus for you. John, will you take 15 and join me in asking Kate, Jack, and Emma to do the same?

Thanks for lunch, Luke—that’s generous, but I’d rather keep the lake healthy and give everyone, including you, an equal share. My family has fished here for generations, and our village depends on it. If we each take 10 tons, we’ll earn $10,000 apiece, leave 50 tons, and start next month back at 100. We can repeat that every month without needing a lean month to recover. I propose a 50-ton total cap, split equally, with a check-in after each harvest. John, would you support 10 tons each instead?

Thanks for lunch, Luke, but I’m with Emma: I’ll take 10 tons. Your plan gives the four of us an extra $5,000 now, but the smaller harvest next month cancels that gain for the group—and leaves you unpaid this month. I’d rather we all earn steadily and keep the lake full. My family taught me to leave enough for the next catch; our village relies on that. Can we agree to 10 tons each this month and review everyone’s catches together afterward? John, are you on board?

I’m on board with 10 tons each, and that’s what I’ll select. Luke, thanks for the offer, but you’re part of this fishing community now—you should have an equal share, not sit out to give us a bonus. Leaving 50 tons means we can keep earning without borrowing from next month. Let’s review the catches together afterward and adjust the total cap if the lake ever starts below 100. Jack, does that work for you? Luke, will you join us?

That works for me, John—I’ll select 10 tons. My family taught me that a good catch should leave us able to fish again, and this agreement does that while giving everyone a fair income. If we ever start below 100 tons, let’s agree on a revised quota before fishing so we leave at least half the starting stock. Luke, you’re welcome at our table and on the lake as an equal. Will you take 10 tons with us?
